Who this is for

You run a home service business and you're good at the work. Your customers are happy. But the money doesn't match the skill, and you've started to think marketing is the gap. You don't want hacks. You want to understand how it works: how to get found, how to price, and how to look like the business people pay more for.

This probably isn't a fit if you want someone to run your marketing while you stay out of it. Everything here is done by you, or done with you.

I was the agency guy. Then I built my own.

For years I ran a marketing agency for home service businesses: SEO, Google Ads, content, the map pack. My clients grew. But I was taking a management fee while they kept what I built, and that math kept bothering me. So I stopped and used every bit of it on my own company.

That company is The Mounting Man. I mount Frame TVs, hang TVs over mantels, drill porcelain tile, and run cable inside the wall. In 2024 I grew fast and learned that volume isn't the goal: I made the money, but contractors ate the profit. So I pruned back, and now I keep more. That's the version of the business I teach.

Google Ads

Google Ads came first.

Before I ranked for anything, Google Ads was the only thing bringing me jobs. Since 2020 I've spent $389,631.54 on Google Ads for The Mounting Man, testing what works so you don't have to. 2024 was the peak, and that year taught me where the waste was. Today my account blocks more than 2,000 negative keywords, which are searches I refuse to pay for. I spend about a third of what I did at the peak, and my profits are better. SEO is huge for me now, but the ads carried the business while it was building.

Step 1

Bid on the high-ticket searches.

Samsung Frame installation, mantel mounts, corporate TV mounting. The jobs that pay well, not the cheapest click.

Step 2

Aim at the neighborhoods that pay.

Put the budget in the premium suburbs and skip the zip codes that don't produce high-ticket work.

Step 3

Cut the waste.

Block the searches that never book. That's where the more than 2,000 negative keywords came from, and now my agents check the search terms for me.

What I learned the expensive way

1

Keep your name in its own campaign.

People searching your business name already found you. Those ads book cheap, so if they're mixed in with everything else, they hide what it really costs to win a new customer.

2

Plain searches book.

The searches that kept booking my appointments were plain ones: the service, "near me," and the city. Build around those before anything clever.

3

Negative keywords cut both ways.

They block the searches that never book. Set too broad, they also block the ones you want. Mine get checked for that too.

4

A booked appointment isn't a paid job.

Google counts booked appointments. Before you call a campaign a winner, check it against the jobs you actually got paid for.

That's money I already spent finding out what works. In Premium, that playbook goes to work in your account. See how Premium works →

The last moat

AI can take the corner office. It can't mount the TV.

A lot of office work is going to AI agents: reports, scheduling, bookkeeping, research. I put one to work in my own business. MoneyPenny runs the office while I run the jobs.

Now ask her to mount a TV over a stone fireplace. She can't. AI can't plumb a house, run a circuit, or get a roof on before the rain. That still takes someone who knows the craft and shows up.

For years the trades got sold as the backup plan. I think they're the part of the economy software can't reach, and the people who do the work should be the ones who get paid for it. The craft is half of it. The other half is the business: ads that bring in the right customers, SEO that keeps them coming, prices that match the work, and AI that handles the office so you can stay on the job. That other half is what I teach.

Ticket growth

I raised my prices every year. My calendar opened up and my tickets went up.

Every year I raised my prices at The Mounting Man, and I set out to master the harder jobs that pay more for about the same time on the wall. Higher rates meant fewer people booking the small jobs, so I wasn't buried in them. That left room on my calendar for the jobs that pay more, like Samsung Frame installs and MantelMounts over the fireplace. I made more per job, and I had more time.

Why raising prices worked

  • I mastered the harder jobs. Stone, fireplaces, Samsung Frame, and MantelMount pay more for about the same time as a basic mount.
  • That changed who I went after. I started targeting richer neighborhoods and the more expensive services, not the lower-priced TV jobs.
  • Higher rates thinned out the small jobs. Fewer people competed for my calendar.
  • The open time went to the bigger jobs. Samsung Frame, MantelMount, and the whole-wall installs fit in on the day the customer wanted.
  • Every job pays more. I price the whole wall, not just the bracket: hidden cords, the soundbar, the outlet, and the right mount.
  • Every price is posted. The customer sees the same price on my site and at booking, so there's no haggling.

TV mounting is a low-ticket trade

TV mounting is about as small as tickets get in home services, and raising prices still changed my business.

If you're in plumbing, HVAC, roofing, or another trade where tickets already start in the thousands, the moves are the same: raise your rates, master the harder jobs that pay more for the same time, price the whole job, post it, and make room for the work that pays. What that does for your business is yours to find out.

Questions

Do I have to be in TV mounting?

No. TV mounting is my trade, so that's where my proof comes from. The system is pricing, Google, ads, and AI for the office, and it's built for home service owners in any trade.

Which door should I start with?

Start where you are. If you want to look around first, Standard is $1/month. If you want the whole system and like to work on your own, the Roadmap Course is $497 once. If you want me working on your business with you every week, Premium is $1,997/month. Any of them is a fine place to start.

Will I make what you made?

My best year with The Mounting Man was $512,022.13. My numbers are my proof, not a promise of yours. Your results depend on your market and your work. What I can promise is that you'll get the same system I used and my help putting it to work in your business.

What does Premium actually do for my business?

We start with your Google Ads. If you run them, your agent audits your account read-only and gives you a keep, cut, fix, and hold report, a restructure plan, and a weekly note on what changed. If you don't, we build the account from the same playbook. Then we build city pages for your service area and set them up for AEO, then we work on your brand. One thing at a time, done with you.

How do the agents find Google Ads waste?

We set up your own AI agent with my Google Ads playbook and give it read-only access to your account. It goes through your spend and search terms and flags the clicks and budget that aren't booking appointments. We go over what it finds together and decide what to cut, one thing at a time.

Do I have to hand over control of my Google Ads?

No. The audit is read-only. Any change to your account is one we agree on together, and you approve it before it happens.

What if I don't run Google Ads yet?

Then we build your account from the same playbook, so you start from what I learned instead of from scratch. We'll also make sure your prices, brand, and Google profile are ready before real money goes into ads.

What does "founding member" mean in Premium?

Premium is new, and the founding members are the first people in. Right now that gets you a lot of my time: weekly live calls, my personal number, and hands-on help. As the group grows, how I give that time may change. Everything included stays included for as long as you stay subscribed.

Is this done-for-you?

No. It's done with you. We pick one thing at a time, whatever matters most for your business right now, and work on it together until it's handled. Then we move to the next one.

SEO, AEO (showing up when people ask AI for a recommendation), Facebook ads, and anything in the High-Ticket Service Academy or in how I built The Mounting Man. I'll also help you build your own AI agents to take care of your business.

The course is the full system, built for owners who want to work it on their own. It's $497 one time with lifetime access, and it doesn't include access to me: no calls, no DMs, and no Q&A.
